text.en: A rich man visits his birthplace to put right something he did long ago.

The narrator and his friend Aditya, a successful man building a new factory, stop at a fork on the highway. Aditya chooses to revisit Bramhapur, the town of his birth, and there takes out a packet and hands it to a gentleman, saying it is from Aditya. The jeweller they visit later says the article is an antique.
Everyone makes mistakes, but a good person tries to rectify them. The story, told by Satyajit Ray, shows regret, honesty and the courage to repay a wrong. The attic was a favourite place for the children.
Look for how the narrator slowly reveals the past through dialogue. Learn the words bifurcate, antique, affluent and rectify. (The exact details of the childhood incident are told in the story itself; read it in your book.)
